DevOps internship, remote and open worldwide

SkillMe's DevOps internship is remote and open worldwide: 4 weeks, one reviewed milestone a week, about 2–3 hours each. You containerise an app with Docker, add automated tests and CI/CD with GitHub Actions, and deploy it. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

The DevOps internship in short

In the SkillMe DevOps internship you build one of 3 projects, such as DevDeploy: Automated Multi-Stage Docker & CI/CD Pipeline Hub, a project where you take a tiny web app and learn to containerise it, test it automatically, and deploy it to the internet on every push. In week 1 you write a tiny notes web app, put it on GitHub, and package it into a Docker container that runs the same way on any machine. By week 4 you complete the pipeline: every push to main that passes CI is deployed to a free host and becomes live on a public URL. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

What you build

One of 3 real projects, built over four weeks

You are assigned one of these projects when you start, and build it milestone by milestone.

DevDeploy: Automated Multi-Stage Docker & CI/CD Pipeline Hub

Take a tiny web app and learn to containerise it, test it automatically, and deploy it to the internet on every push.

  1. W1Git Basics & Your First Dockerfile
  2. W2App + Database with Docker Compose
  3. W3Automated Tests & CI with GitHub Actions
  4. W4Auto-Deploy to the Cloud & Health Checks

InfraGuard: Microservices Orchestration & Infrastructure as Code

Build two small services that work together, run them with Docker Compose behind a gateway, and describe the setup as code.

  1. W1Two Small Services in Containers
  2. W2Orchestrate Everything with Docker Compose
  3. W3Nginx Gateway & Handling Failures
  4. W4Infrastructure as Code with Terraform (Local)

UptimeWatch: Website Uptime Monitor & Status Page

Build a tool that checks whether your favourite websites are up, runs automatically on a schedule, and publishes a public status page.

  1. W1Uptime Checker Script & Git
  2. W2Containerise the Checker & Save Results
  3. W3Scheduled Checks & Tests with GitHub Actions
  4. W4Public Status Page & Downtime Alerts
Week by week

What each week of the DevOps internship covers

Shown for DevDeploy: Automated Multi-Stage Docker & CI/CD Pipeline Hub. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Git Basics & Your First Dockerfile

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Write a tiny notes web app, put it on GitHub, and package it into a Docker container that runs the same way on any machine. This is the foundation every later week builds on.

    What you learn

    • A basic Git workflow: init, add, commit, push and meaningful commit messages
    • What containers and images are, and why teams use them
    • Writing a Dockerfile with FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN, EXPOSE and CMD
    • Running containers with port mapping and reading their logs

    What you submit

    • A small web app with /, /notes and /health routes
    • A Dockerfile and .dockerignore
    • A public GitHub repo with several meaningful commits
    • A README with build and run instructions
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • docker build finishes without errors
    • The running container responds on /, /notes and /health in the browser
    • The repo has at least 4 commits with clear messages
    • Someone else could run the app using only the README commands

    Stretch goal: Use a slim base image (for example python:3.12-slim or node:20-alpine) and compare image sizes with docker images.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    App + Database with Docker Compose

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Real apps need a database. This week you add PostgreSQL and run both the app and database together with one Docker Compose command, so notes are saved permanently instead of disappearing on restart.

    What you learn

    • Defining multiple services in a docker-compose.yml file
    • How containers talk to each other by service name on a Compose network
    • Keeping data safe with named volumes
    • Configuring apps with environment variables and a .env file

    What you submit

    • A docker-compose.yml running the app and PostgreSQL
    • Notes saved in the database through POST /notes
    • A .env.example file and no real secrets in Git
    • An updated README
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • docker compose up --build starts both services with one command
    • Notes created through the API are returned by GET /notes
    • Notes survive docker compose down followed by docker compose up
    • No passwords are committed to the repo
    • The app does not crash if it starts before the database is ready

    Stretch goal: Add a healthcheck to the db service and make app wait for it using depends_on with condition: service_healthy.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Automated Tests & CI with GitHub Actions

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Set up a pipeline that automatically checks every push: it lints your code, runs tests, and builds the Docker image. You will also switch to a multi-stage Dockerfile so the final image is smaller and cleaner.

    What you learn

    • What Continuous Integration (CI) is and why it catches problems early
    • Writing a GitHub Actions workflow with triggers, jobs and steps
    • Writing a few simple automated tests and running a linter
    • Multi-stage Docker builds to keep production images small

    What you submit

    • A test suite with at least 3 passing tests
    • A GitHub Actions workflow that lints, tests and builds the image
    • A multi-stage Dockerfile
    • Screenshots of a failing and a passing CI run
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • Tests pass locally and in GitHub Actions
    • The workflow runs automatically on push and on pull requests
    • A lint error or failing test makes the workflow fail
    • Invalid input to POST /notes returns a 400 response
    • The README shows a CI status badge

    Stretch goal: Push your image to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io) from the workflow when changes land on main.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    Auto-Deploy to the Cloud & Health Checks

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Complete the pipeline: every push to main that passes CI is deployed to a free host and becomes live on a public URL. You will add health checks and useful logs, then document the whole flow.

    What you learn

    • Continuous Deployment (CD): shipping automatically after tests pass
    • Deploying a Docker container to a free platform such as Render
    • Managing production configuration and secrets on a hosting platform
    • Health checks and structured logs for spotting problems

    What you submit

    • A live public URL for your app
    • A workflow that deploys only after CI passes on main
    • A /health route that checks the database
    • A README with a pipeline diagram and a 60-second demo video
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • The app is reachable at a public URL and can create and list notes
    • Pushing to main with passing tests triggers a deploy automatically
    • A failing test stops the deploy from happening
    • No secrets appear in the repo; the deploy hook and database URL are stored as secrets
    • Request logs are visible on the hosting dashboard

    Stretch goal: Add a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that calls your /health URL every hour and fails (sending you an email) if the site is down.

Is it for you?

Who the DevOps internship is for, and what you leave with

This internship fits you if

  • You know the basics of Docker, GitHub Actions and CI/CD and want a real project to show for it, not more tutorials.
  • You can start at beginner level. Week 1: Write a tiny notes web app, put it on GitHub, and package it into a Docker container that runs the same way on any machine.
  • You want to reach intermediate+ level in four weeks. Week 4: Complete the pipeline: every push to main that passes CI is deployed to a free host and becomes live on a public URL.
  • You can give it about 2-3 hours a week around college or a job, from any country.

How to apply

  1. Take the 5-minute quiz. Eight questions on the basics of Docker, GitHub Actions, CI/CD.
  2. Tell us why you want in. A person reads every application. Anyone can apply, but selection is competitive.
  3. Get shortlisted. If you are selected you hear back within 48 hours and receive your offer letter.
  4. Build and submit weekly. One milestone a week for four weeks, each one reviewed.

DevOps internship: questions and answers

Is the DevOps internship remote?

Yes. It is a fully remote DevOps internship, open to students in any country, at about 2–3 hours a week.

What does a remote DevOps intern do here?

You take a small app from code to production: write a Dockerfile, run the app and a database with Docker Compose, add automated tests and CI with GitHub Actions, then deploy it with health checks. Other projects cover an Nginx gateway with Terraform, or a scheduled uptime monitor with a public status page.

What will I build in the DevOps internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: DevDeploy: Automated Multi-Stage Docker & CI/CD Pipeline Hub, InfraGuard: Microservices Orchestration & Infrastructure as Code or UptimeWatch: Website Uptime Monitor & Status Page. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the DevOps internship?

The DevOps internship works with Docker, GitHub Actions and CI/CD. Week 1: a basic Git workflow: init, add, commit, push and meaningful commit messages; what containers and images are, and why teams use them. Week 2: defining multiple services in a docker-compose.yml file; how containers talk to each other by service name on a Compose network. Week 3: what Continuous Integration (CI) is and why it catches problems early; writing a GitHub Actions workflow with triggers, jobs and steps. Week 4: continuous Deployment (CD): shipping automatically after tests pass; deploying a Docker container to a free platform such as Render.

Do I need experience to apply for the DevOps internship?

You need the basics of Docker, GitHub Actions and CI/CD, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you write a tiny notes web app, put it on GitHub, and package it into a Docker container that runs the same way on any machine. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each DevOps milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of DevDeploy: Automated Multi-Stage Docker & CI/CD Pipeline Hub, that means: docker build finishes without errors; the running container responds on /, /notes and /health in the browser; the repo has at least 4 commits with clear messages; someone else could run the app using only the README commands. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the DevOps internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Built a small web app and packaged it into a Docker container; Wrote a Dockerfile and .dockerignore and ran the app with port mapping; Managed the project with Git using small, meaningful commits; Ran a web app and PostgreSQL together using Docker Compose; Used named volumes and environment variables to persist data and keep secrets out of Git; Added startup retries so the app handles a slow database gracefully; Set up a CI pipeline with GitHub Actions that lints, tests and builds a Docker image; Wrote automated tests and added input validation to a web API; Reduced image size by converting to a multi-stage Dockerfile; Built a full CI/CD pipeline that tests and deploys a Dockerised app on every push; Deployed a containerised web app with a hosted PostgreSQL database to a free cloud platform; Added database-aware health checks and request logging for production monitoring.

What are the other projects in the DevOps internship?

InfraGuard: Microservices Orchestration & Infrastructure as Code: Build two small services that work together, run them with Docker Compose behind a gateway, and describe the setup as code. UptimeWatch: Website Uptime Monitor & Status Page: Build a tool that checks whether your favourite websites are up, runs automatically on a schedule, and publishes a public status page. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the DevOps internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based: 8–10 interns are picked each month from those who complete the internship and hold an issued certificate. It is not paid to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
